BE NICE:
The individuals presented in these videos may be suffering from the effects of alcohol, drug abuse, a mental health disorder or simply having a bad day. The videos should NOT be presumed to be representative of their general behavior. Everyone deserves to be treated with respect. 

RIGHT TO BE FORGOTTEN:
Midwest Safety practices the "Right to be Forgotten." If you were the suspect in a lower-level offense, you may email our board to request removal. 
Email: contact@midwest-safety.com

This suspect, whose real name is Khadija Terry, has an extensive criminal history involving multiple retail thefts and fraud cases. In 2015, when she was 21 years old, Khadija attempted to use fraudulent gift cards at a Walgreens in Indiana. When police were called to the Walgreens, they found 32 MasterCard and Visa gift cards in her purse. Before being brought in for questioning, Khadija told police she was pregnant and experiencing pain, so she needed to go to the hospital. However, on the way to the hospital, she jumped out of the ambulance. When medics and police restrained her, she allegedly struck an officer in the process. She later was determined to not be pregnant and was charged with felony fraud, felony battery, felony identity deception, and resisting. She took a plea deal, pleading guilty to fraud while all other charges were dismissed and was sentenced to two hundred seventy days in jail. Then in 2017, Khadija allegedly attempted to shoplift $1,140 worth of merchandise at a Dick's sporting goods in Indiana. When police arrived, she reportedly fled in a stolen vehicle, and then allegedly tried to run over police officers and rammed a squad. She was then charged with two counts of felony attempted murder, three counts of resisting law enforcement, felony attempted theft, and two counts of felony attempted battery with a deadly weapon. She took a plea deal, pleading guilty to one count of resisting, and both counts of attempted battery with a deadly weapon while all other charges were dismissed. She was then sentenced to seven years in prison. Exactly seven years later in July 2024 when she was released, the incident in this body cam footage took place in Illinois. For this incident, she was charged with two counts of resisting a peace officer, attempted retail theft, unlawful use of identification, obstruction of identification, unauthorized use of handicapped parking, and operating a motor vehicle with no valid driver's license for over six months. Then just four months after this incident in November 2024, Khadija was allegedly involved in yet another retail theft incident at a mall in Illinois. She reportedly fled from police in an Audi Q-5 when they attempted to perform a traffic stop and then crashed into a Lexus SUV. Officers then removed her from the Audi and after being transported to a nearby hospital, she allegedly caused approximately $7,000 worth of damage to a hospital bed. A short clip from this incident details her attitude when police attempt to get her out of the vehicle. I'm about myself. I'm about myself. What am I under arrest for? You just fled from me, okay? You're under arrest. You back into my car and then you fled and then you caused another crash. You ready? You ready? So darn. She was subsequently charged with two counts of felony aggravated fleeing and eluding, felony criminal damage to property, resisting, driving with a suspended license, improper turn, and failure to signal in a motor vehicle. She took a plea deal, pleading guilty to one count of aggravated fleeing and eluding while all other charges were dismissed. She was sentenced to 30 months in prison. You notice the way she just casually strolls past those officers as soon as they make contact? That's not confusion. That's experience. That's someone hoping confidence buys time because a quick, quiet getaway is often playing Then the investigation starts and one officer positions near the front of her car, and I'll be honest, I never like that spot because some people will drive straight through you to escape, and that vest will not protect you. Now watch the moment she's told she's detained, she goes back to her car and starts changing clothes, but she's also reaching inside that car, and this is where a stop turns tense real fast. Because we don't know if it's a hoodie or a weapon, even retired, my pulse jumps watching it because cops don't just rewatch scenes like this, we relive them and remember what they feel like. Instead of running, the strategy changes, you start seeing hesitation, confusion, and sudden medical issues right when the cuffs appear. It's not really about passing out, it's a last second attempt to regain control of a situation that just got real. Because for some people, the theft wasn't the stressful part being held accountable is, and officers recognize that immediately. Which is why they keep moving forward even while someone is screaming. Not to punish someone, but to bring the moment back under control before it turns into something nobody can undo.
